messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: continuous-batcher pod crashloop detected in us-west-2-prod (svc=continuous-batcher). 5x container restarts in 2m, OOMKilled + CUDA errors in logs. Auto-escalating to #eng-oncall.

maya: seeing the page. latency spike on production /generate, tailing logs now. customers showing 502/timeout.

sam: confirmed node flaps reported by node-exporter: gpu-node-12 lost and rejoined, K8s restarted 3 pods.

maya: logs show repeated cudaErrorIllegalInstruction followed by oom_kill:
```
E cuda: illegal instruction at 0x7f3a...
I kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (continuous-batcher) score 987 
```

jordan: that's the same pattern we saw with prefetch growth last month. KV cache + continuous batching + long sequences -> memory spiral.

maya: rolling mitigation plan: 1) route traffic off us-west-2 pool 2) scale batcher down / reduce max_batch_size 3) disable prefetch temporarily 4) cordon/evict bad node. doing 1 now.

sam: @maya how are you routing? I can flip route if you want.

maya: using runtime-routing CLI: `redwood route update --pool us-west-2 --weight 0.2` to shift to dedicated fallback pool. doing that.

maya: Route update applied. Traffic to batcher in us-west reduced to 20%. latency dropped a bit. still seeing OOMs on remaining pods.

jordan: we should kill prefetch threads. there's a flag on the service: `--enable-prefetch=false`. can we restart with that?

maya: prepping a restart with new args. will do rolling restart one pod at a time.

aaron: heads-up I'm incoming to take handoff in 10m. if you need me to continue mitigation ping.

sre-bot: ACTION: Node cordon scheduled for gpu-node-12. Reason: repeated GPU page faults + kernel OOMs.

maya: cordon succeeded. draining now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

sam: drain stuck on continuous-batcher-78c9 (eviction blocked by local emptyDir mount). workaround: `kubectl delete pod continuous-batcher-78c9 --grace-period=30` to force.

maya: forced delete executed. pod rescheduled on gpu-node-15.

jordan: after restart with `--enable-prefetch=false` the new pod failed with CUDA illegal instruction during model init. might be a mismatched CUDA runtime on that node image.

maya: that explains the illegal instruction -- node's driver is older. checking node image versions across pool.

sam: node-exporter shows gpu-node-15 driver 470.x, gpu-node-12 driver 515.x. model binary built for 515+?

jordan: yes binary is optimized with cuda 11.8 kernels; 470s can hit illegal instruction. we need to avoid scheduling to older drivers or use fallback CPU/quantized model.

maya: short-term: evict pods from 470 driver nodes, set nodeSelector toleration to avoid older drivers. applying taint: `kubectl label node gpu-node-15 redwood/cuda=old` and update scheduler affinity.

sam: applied label. scheduler will avoid until we roll nodes. rolling update of nodes to standard image planned.

aaron: taking over oncall now. leaving notes: we've reduced traffic to 20%, cordoned bad node, forced delete blocked pod, disabled prefetch, labeled old-driver nodes to avoid scheduling. next: 1) scale dedicated fallback pool up 2) enable temporary model fallback (quantized) 3) notify customers.

lina: I'm on rotations for customer comms. need impact window and affected customers list.

maya: impact: ~3% of requests in the last 15m saw 5-10s latency or 502. Major traffic was degraded for some enterprise customers on us-west-2 routing. Preparing list from proxy logs now.

sam: quick mitigation to prevent future illegal instruction: update runtime to select compatible model variant when node driver < 500. patch ready: `if node.cuda_driver < 500 then model_variant = quantized-v1`

jordan: pushing that patch to canary now.

sre-bot: DEPLOY: canary deploy started for runtime routing policy at 1715004378 by jordan.

maya: canary looks stable on nodes with older drivers. no illegal instruction in 2 restarts.

lina: draft outgoing: "We've observed transient errors and latency affecting some requests in us-west-2 due to GPU driver mismatches and continuous-batcher memory growth. We've shifted traffic and applied mitigations; full service restored to >98% while we roll nodes and deploy a compatibility fallback. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem." Approve?

aaron: approve. add ETA for full rollout of node images ~4h.

lina: sending notice to customers and SAs.

sam: next actions for eng-runtime: run targeted memprof on batcher to collect KV cache growth traces, add guardrails on KV prefetch (hard cap), and add metric for per-pod prefetch usage.

maya: creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + infra. ticket: INC-2026-0421. notes: paging, OOMs, CUDA illegal instruction, node-driver mismatch, prefetch growth, mitigation steps taken.

aaron: I'm logging a handback to oncall rotation at 1715004440. @lina @jordan continue with postmortem and infra rollout. I'll be available for escalations.

sre-bot: HANDOFF: oncall changed from maya -> aaron at 1715004440.

maya: thanks all. saving traces and heapdumps to s3://redwood-incident/INC-2026-0421/ for postmortem.

jordan: leaving a quick reproduction note: long sequences + prefetch enabled + high concurrency causes kv-cache to grow without bound under rare cache-eviction bug. steps to reproduce attached in ticket.

lina: closing the loop with legal and support. will collect customer impact and timeline for postmortem.

sam: follow-ups: - backfill node-driver check into deployment pipeline - add runtime guard to select quantized model on older drivers - hard cap on kv prefetch memory - add alert when a single batcher pod uses >75% GPU mem for >30s

maya: thanks team. I'll hand off the logs and open PR for the prefetch cap.

incident-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: INC-2026-0421 created, severity: P2, assignees: eng-runtime, infra, SRE.

aaron: handoff complete. I'll monitor for 1h and then move to watch.
